content:
alex.w: Heads-up — the weekly GPU-hour forecast is drifting vs actuals. our 7d MA is ~9% below real usage during weekday mornings for the last 10 days.

maria.c: Wow that's sizable. any idea what's biasing the MA?

alex.w: Quick root cause candidate: our sampler weights long-tail chat sessions equally with short completions, so p50 token/sec moves slower than the true p95 traffic spike. also a config change last week lowered sampling rate from 30m->2h.

jonathan: That explains it. We should avoid under-reacting to short high-load windows. Thinking: use a 24h exponentially-weighted smoothing on p90 tokens/sec with alpha=0.3 and add a safety buffer of +10% for peak provisioning.

maria.c: Can you sketch the config you'd want?

jonathan: Sure — pseudo config:
```yaml
forecast:
  metric: tokens_per_sec_p90
  smoothing:
    method: exponential
    alpha: 0.30
    lookback: 24h
  buffer_pct: 0.10  # safety margin for morning peaks
```

alex.w: Doing the back-of-envelope: current p90 = 120k tokens/sec across region -> target capacity = 120k * (1 + 0.10) = 132k tokens/sec. With our baseline GPU throughput ~22k tokens/sec per machine, that's ~6 machines (132k/22k ≈ 6). Previously planner picked 5.

sam.k: Cost note: bumping to 6 reserved GPUs moves reserved spend +12% for that pool. But it avoids tail throttles that cost 10–15% of requests failing back to slower models. tradeoff seems net-positive.

infra-bot: capacity-scan: region us-west - current reserved GPUs:5 - suggested:6 - delta:+1 - reason: p90 smoothing delta.

maria.c: Can we do a temporary micro-mitigation while we tweak smoothing? e.g., adaptive packing + partial preemptible fallback for non-SLA traffic.

alex.w: Yes — enable packing tweaks for short requests (<=64 tokens) to reduce tail load, and route non-critical routes to preemptible. small config diff: `route.allow_preemptible: true` for tag=nonprod and tag=async.

jonathan: Also add a short-term tweak to sampling cadence back to 30m for the next 72h so forecasts re-align faster. Then revert after model stabilizes.

maria.c: I'll open a runbook step and a quick sim in the capacity sandbox. planning to run: `./tools/capacity-sim --window 7d --smoothing exp:0.3 --buffer 0.10`

sam.k: If the sim confirms, we should do a controlled rollout: 1) enable exp smoothing in staging, 2) nudged reserved pool +1 in us-west, 3) enable packing, 4) watch SLOs for 4 hours.

alex.w: Agreed. @maria.c can you create the infra ticket and tag ops?

maria.c: Created INFRA-4321 and linked the sim output: https://boards.internal/INFRA-4321 — assigning to @jonathan and @sam.k.

jonathan: I'll take the smoothing deploy. will add unit tests for smoothing math and a small dashboard showing p50/p90/p99 comparisons.

sam.k: I'll own the cost impact calc and the staged reserved bump.

alex.w: Thanks team. small ask: add a nightly check that alerts if forecast vs actual diverges >7% for two consecutive days. reduces surprise.

maria.c: Added to the ticket. closing loop after sim completes. :thumbsup:
